stem: $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral. The point $E$ lies on ray $AB$ with $E \notin \overline{AB}$, $m(\text{arc } AB) = {=p}^\circ$ and $m(\angle CBE) = {=e}^\circ$. Find $m(\angle BDC)$.
solution: $\angle ADB$ is an inscribed angle subtending arc $AB$, so $m(\angle ADB) = \frac{1}{2} \times {=p}^\circ = {=h}^\circ$.
$\angle CBE$ is an exterior angle at vertex $B$ of the cyclic quadrilateral, so $m(\angle CDA) = m(\angle CBE) = {=e}^\circ$ (Corollary).
notes: Mirrors book example 2 with new numbers; D lies so that ray DB is inside angle ADC.
